issue_text: gitStatus's parse-failure guard `if v == ""` (setup.go:211-215, the "Could not parse the git version" remediation) and parseGitVersion's fallback `return ""` (setup.go:233) are never exercised by any test, and the guard is deletable with the whole suite still green. The gitversion_test.go case named "unparseable" (input "git version ... : not a version banner") does NOT reach this branch: parseGitVersion scans for a token equal to "version" and returns the NEXT field, and the input "not a version banner" contains the word "version" at index 2, so parseGitVersion returns "banner" (verified by probe), not "". The observed VersionOK=false / action-mentions-2.31 outcome is produced by the numeric-comparison-failure path (atLeastVersion("banner",..)==false), not the parse-failure path the case name implies. A side effect: in that scenario gitStatus sets status.Version="banner" (line 216) BEFORE the numeric check, so the JSON contract would report the git version as literally "banner". The true empty-parse input (e.g. output "git version" with nothing after it, probe returns "") is what the case intended and is uncovered.
why_real: Verified by (a) running parseGitVersion on the exact test input -> "banner", and on "git version\n" -> ""; (b) coverage marking setup.go:233 (parseGitVersion return "") and setup.go:526-equivalent (gitStatus v=="" remediation) uncovered. Deleting the `if v == ""` block leaves all tests passing because no test feeds an input that makes parseGitVersion return "". This is a genuine untested guard on the git-version JSON contract plus a test whose name asserts coverage it does not provide, and it lets a bogus token be surfaced as ToolStatus.Version.
tests_checked: gitversion_test.go TestGitStatusReportsTheVersionAndTheMinimum case {"unparseable","not a version banner\n"} (line 25) and TestGitStatusAbsentIsUnchanged; no test supplies output that yields empty parseGitVersion. Confirmed via added throwaway probe test and go tool cover.

issue_text: The positive ('present') detection paths for three prerequisites that feed the JSON contract (Prerequisites.*.Present, Standalone.MissingForFullMetaswarm, FullMetaswarmReady/AdvisoryOnly) are entirely untested and are deletable with the suite still green: beadsStatus's bd-CLI branch (setup.go:155-157 `lookup("bd")`), metaswarmStatus's sibling/plugin loop (setup.go:165-173, i.e. ../metaswarm, .claude/plugins/metaswarm, .codex/plugins/metaswarm), and superpowersStatus's directory loop positive return (setup.go:143-146). Coverage confirms lines 156, 166-172, 145 are all cov0. The only Check-level test drives every one of these to the absent branch, so a regression that mis-names the CLI (e.g. lookup("beads") instead of "bd"), points metaswarm detection at the wrong path, or breaks the plugin-dir candidates would report an installed prerequisite as absent (or an absent one as present) and no test would fail. Detection accuracy is the whole job of this package and these branches have zero guarding assertions.
why_real: Category-2 (invariant nothing holds): I confirmed via go tool cover that setup.go:145,156,166-172 are uncovered, and that deleting metaswarmStatus's for-loop or beadsStatus's bd branch leaves TestCheckPreservesRepoFieldsAndAddsPrerequisiteStatuses passing (that test only exercises the all-absent outcome). Inverting `if repoHasBeads`/`if repoHasMetaswarm` IS caught by the MissingForFullMetaswarm DeepEqual assertion, but the CLI-lookup / sibling-dir / plugin-dir 'present' outcomes have no positive fixture at all, so a false-absent regression in real deployments ships silently. Not speculation: the branches are demonstrably deletable against the green suite.
tests_checked: setup_test.go TestCheckPreservesRepoFieldsAndAddsPrerequisiteStatuses (lines 12-61): LookupPath returns error for 'bd', no .beads dir, no sibling metaswarm, no superpowers dirs -> all three resolve to the Action branch; assertions only check the absent outcome (lines 46-59) and MissingForFullMetaswarm order. No test in the package builds a fixture where bd is on PATH, a ../metaswarm or plugin metaswarm dir exists, or a superpowers plugin dir exists.
